anomalies.evidence: evidence/CEO-m2-staffing.png and evidence/CEO-m2-staffing-run1.png (two independent runs, same result). Measured by decoding the PNGs: in the scatter band (y 900–1140) and the histogram band (y 1290–1510) the only non-background pixels are the axis labels, the grid baseline and one dashed reference line. Controls that rule out my detector and a one-off flake: evidence/CEO-m0-staffing.png and evidence/FINANCE-m0-staffing.png show a dense point cloud and eight solid bars in the same bands, and evidence/CEO-m2-exec-overview.png / CEO-m2-discounts.png / CEO-m2-trends.png all show their bars and lines at mode 2. The payload is not the suspect: report_m06_staffing builds 717 scatter points and 8 histogram buckets (supabase/migrations/20260916083000_module11_d2_rpcs_executive_fixes.sql:1449-1454), the runner recorded charts=2, console_errors=0 and rows=50/50 on the same load.

blind_spot: This evidence cannot say whether a real CEO at mode 2 sees מ6's charts empty, or only a Playwright full-page capture does. Playwright resizes the viewport to the full page height before shooting, which re-measures every recharts ResponsiveContainer and restarts its animation — so a capture can freeze the series at frame 0 while a human at a fixed 1280×800 window sees them fine. The check that settles it, and it is one action: open http://localhost:5189/reports?tab=exec&report=staffing as the CEO with onboarding mode 2, without resizing, and look at the two cards — or read the sr-only twin table inside [data-testid="chart-card-scatter"], which holds the same rows the SVG should draw. What makes the artifact theory incomplete, and why I graded it blocker anyway: the identical capture path produced full bars on CEO m0, on FINANCE m0/m2 and on the three other exec surfaces at mode 2, and it produced the same empty plot twice on this one.
